H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper says Mode_Control_Algorithm specifies four states, wait/manual/autocontrol init/autocontrol, and also an Ask_StartAC submode.

G_guards_arith.evidence: The Algorithm EFSM contains the composed guard CA_backManual OR CB_backManual OR CP_backManual OR CC_backManual -> CA_mode = Manual.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Fault handling activates alarm signals and releases CARA control; other mode behavior sets pump speed by switch or by external control voltage, and the algorithm keeps infusion data in log files.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: On pump complications, control reverts to the manual operator/caregiver; any of four backManual flags can force CA_mode back to Manual.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Mode names and Ask_StartAC appear in the Hermes section, while manual/autocontrol semantics, alarms, release of control, and backManual guards are described earlier in separate CARA overview and EFSM sections.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as manual mode, autocontrol mode, pump fault, complications, and releases its control imply control-priority and failover rules beyond the literal labels.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are narrative prose: alarm signals are activated, pump speed is set by switch or control voltage, setpoint can be changed, and software releases control; these are not co-located in a state/action table.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: CA_backManual OR CB_backManual OR CP_backManual OR CC_backManual is a multi-variable boolean guard.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: The paper gives a shallow Mode_Control_Algorithm hierarchy and Ask_StartAC submode, but does not document parent-mode entry/during/exit behavior beyond its substates.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: Any of four EFSMs can trigger the algorithm to switch to Manual, forming a cross-cutting recovery rule that a flat baseline would likely duplicate across algorithm modes.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is one shallow composite Mode_Control_Algorithm with an Ask_StartAC submode, but no deep non-trivial initialization chain is documented.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The sample has one notable composed boolean guard over four backManual variables, but not several arithmetic guards.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The backManual rule applies as a global forced return to Manual from the mode-control algorithm when any of several modules requests it.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs include appropriate alarms, messages, log-file tracking, and release of control, but some effectors are concrete, such as pump switch and control voltage.

key_nl_quotes: The pump has two modes, manual and autocontrol. In manual mode, the pump speed is set with a switch built into the pump. In autocontrol mode, the pumping speed is set by a control voltage from an external source.
CA_backManual OR CB_backManual OR CP_backManual OR CC-backManual -> CA-mode = Manual.
one_line_pitch: This is a compact but high-value stress test because mode hierarchy, multi-source manual fallback, fault-triggered alarm/control-release actions, and cross-cutting back-to-manual logic are scattered across the paper.
rationale: The sample has a real EFSM mode controller with manual/autocontrol operational semantics, a shallow hierarchical submode, and a composed backManual guard over four modules. Its strongest stress-test value is the global recovery pattern: pump complications and any backManual request force control back to Manual while also involving alarms and release of CARA control. The information is distributed across overview, EFSM architecture, and Hermes model sections, making it a strong baseline-trap case rather than a single-table extraction.
